protocol: PDF-only questions, expected answers, exact source excerpts and exhaustive relevant document-page labels pre-registered before execution. Document keys identify original bundled bytes. Pages are 1-based.

AI.filename: AI and Machine Learning Course Guide.pdf

questions.question: What are the Python Programming course completion requirements?

expected.answer: Submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone.

excerpts: To complete the Python Programming course, submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone project.

questions.question: What percentage of the Python Programming final mark comes from graded labs and from the capstone project?

expected.answer: Graded labs: 60%. Capstone project: 40%.

excerpts: Graded labs account for 60% of the course mark.
The capstone project accounts for 40% of the course mark.

questions.question: Where and how do I submit each graded Python lab, including the required files?

expected.answer: Submit in LMS Assessments as a ZIP containing Python source files and a short README.

excerpts: Submit each lab through the LMS Assessments area as a ZIP archive containing Python source files and a short README.

questions.question: Which submission slot is for the Python capstone project, and what three things should I include?

expected.answer: Use the Capstone submission slot and include Python source, test files, and instructions for running the project.

excerpts: Upload the capstone to the Capstone submission slot. Include your Python source, test files, and instructions for running the project.

questions.question: How long does the introductory Python Programming course run?

expected.answer: Six weeks.

excerpts: Python Programming is a six-week foundation course for new programmers.

questions.question: What practical programming tasks do new Python learners perform?

expected.answer: Write and debug small command-line programs, organize code into reusable functions, and read structured files.

excerpts: Learners write and debug small command-line programs, organize code into reusable functions, and read structured files.

questions.question: What topics does Python Programming cover in weeks 3 and 4?

expected.answer: Functions, modules, files, exceptions, and debugging.

excerpts: Weeks 3 and 4 cover functions, modules, files, exceptions, and debugging.

questions.question: In which week of the Python course are unit tests and code review introduced?

expected.answer: Week 5.

excerpts: Week 5 introduces unit tests and code review.

questions.question: How many Python capstone resubmissions are available, and when?

expected.answer: One resubmission, after written feedback.

excerpts: A capstone resubmission is available once after written feedback.

questions.question: Where and when will I see the Python course completion record?

expected.answer: In LMS Results after the course coordinator verifies the completion conditions.

excerpts: The completion record appears in the LMS Results area after the course coordinator verifies the conditions.

questions.question: Does a Python capstone Pass by itself satisfy course completion requirements?

expected.answer: A capstone Pass alone is insufficient. The requirements also include all four graded labs and at least 70% overall.

excerpts: To complete the Python Programming course, submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone project.

questions.question: What share of the overall mark is the Python capstone worth, and what separate capstone outcome is required for completion?

expected.answer: The capstone is worth 40% of the mark and must separately earn a Pass.

excerpts: The capstone project accounts for 40% of the course mark.
To complete the Python Programming course, submit all four graded labs, achieve at least 70% overall, and earn a Pass on the capstone project.

questions.question: How is the AI and Machine Learning final grade split between quizzes, the notebook, and the capstone report?

expected.answer: Two quizzes are worth 20% combined, the modeling notebook 35%, and the capstone report 45%.

excerpts: The AI and Machine Learning final mark consists of two quizzes worth 20% combined, a modeling notebook worth 35%, and a capstone report worth 45%.

questions.question: What goes in the final capstone write-up for the AI course?

expected.answer: Dataset description, a baseline model, validation results, and a discussion of limitations.

excerpts: The capstone report must include the dataset description, a baseline model, validation results, and a discussion of limitations.

questions.question: What file formats are required for the AI modeling notebook and capstone report, and can I submit them together in one slot?

expected.answer: The notebook is IPYNB and the report is PDF. They go in separate LMS Assessments slots.

excerpts: Submit the modeling notebook as an IPYNB file and the capstone report as a PDF in separate LMS Assessments slots.

questions.question: Which two prerequisites should I understand before starting AI and Machine Learning?

expected.answer: Python functions and basic descriptive statistics.

excerpts: Before starting, learners should understand Python functions and basic descriptive statistics.

questions.question: How many weeks is the AI and Machine Learning course?

expected.answer: Eight weeks.

excerpts: AI and Machine Learning is an eight-week applied course.

questions.question: In the AI classification workshop, which models should I compare and which results should I report?

expected.answer: Compare a logistic regression baseline with a decision tree. Report precision, recall, and a confusion matrix.

excerpts: For classification workshops, compare a logistic regression baseline with a decision tree. Report precision, recall, and the confusion matrix.

questions.question: What five areas do the AI and Machine Learning modules cover?

expected.answer: Dataset preparation, classification, regression, validation, and responsible model reporting.

excerpts: Modules cover dataset preparation, classification, regression, validation, and responsible model reporting.

questions.question: What three ongoing learning resources are listed in the AI guide?

expected.answer: A glossary, weekly notebook walkthroughs, and an evaluation checklist.

excerpts: The learning resources include a glossary, weekly notebook walkthroughs, and an evaluation checklist.

questions.question: For eligible assignments, how late can I submit and what is the penalty, including partial periods?

expected.answer: For assignments marked eligible, up to 48 hours after the deadline. Deduct 10 percentage points per 24-hour period or part thereof.

excerpts: For assignments marked eligible for late submission, a learner may submit up to 48 hours after the deadline. The penalty is 10 percentage points per 24-hour period or part thereof.

questions.question: If I catch up by replaying a session, does that count toward my live attendance?

expected.answer: Watching a recording does not count toward live attendance.

excerpts: Watching a recording does not count toward live attendance.

questions.question: What minimum percentage of scheduled live sessions must I attend, and how long must I stay for a session to count?

expected.answer: Attend at least 75% of scheduled live sessions. Be present for at least half of the scheduled duration for a session to count.

excerpts: Learners must attend at least 75% of scheduled live sessions. A live session counts when the learner is present for at least half of its scheduled duration.

questions.question: Where will live attendance records appear, and how soon after a session?

expected.answer: In LMS Attendance within two working days of a session.

excerpts: Attendance records appear in the LMS Attendance area within two working days of a session.

questions.question: What is the deadline and LMS location for requesting an assessment review after the grade is released?

expected.answer: Request in LMS Support within five working days after the grade is released.

excerpts: Request an assessment review in the LMS Support area within five working days after the grade is released.

questions.question: What information should I include in an assessment review request?

expected.answer: The assessment name, the rubric criterion, and a short explanation of the issue.

excerpts: Include the assessment name, the rubric criterion, and a short explanation of the issue.

questions.question: If the LMS is unavailable before an assignment deadline, whom should I contact and what should I send?

expected.answer: Contact course support and include the error details before the deadline where possible.

excerpts: If the LMS is unavailable, contact course support and include the error details before the deadline where possible.

questions.question: What proof of delivery should I keep after I submit graded work in the LMS?

expected.answer: Keep the timestamped submission receipt.

excerpts: Keep the timestamped submission receipt as proof of delivery.

questions.question: How do I ask for ordinary learning help instead of an assessment review?

expected.answer: Use the LMS Support area and select the Course Support category.

excerpts: Request an assessment review in the LMS Support area within five working days after the grade is released.
Requests for general learning support can be submitted in the same area using the Course Support category.

questions.question: Compare capstone weighting for Python Programming and AI and Machine Learning.

expected.answer: Python Programming capstone project: 40%. AI and Machine Learning capstone report: 45%.

excerpts: The capstone project accounts for 40% of the course mark.
The AI and Machine Learning final mark consists of two quizzes worth 20% combined, a modeling notebook worth 35%, and a capstone report worth 45%.

questions.question: How long are the Python Programming and AI and Machine Learning courses?

expected.answer: Python Programming: six weeks. AI and Machine Learning: eight weeks.

excerpts: Python Programming is a six-week foundation course for new programmers.
AI and Machine Learning is an eight-week applied course.

questions.question: Where is a graded Python lab submitted, and how soon do live attendance records appear?

expected.answer: Submit the Python lab in LMS Assessments. Attendance records appear in LMS Attendance within two working days of a session.

excerpts: Submit each lab through the LMS Assessments area as a ZIP archive containing Python source files and a short README.
